question: What is the difference between HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3?
answer:
**HTTP/1.1**: one request per TCP connection at a time (head-of-line blocking), keep-alive allows reuse but is still sequential.

**HTTP/2**: multiplexing — multiple requests in parallel over one TCP connection, header compression (HPACK), server push. Still has head-of-line blocking at the TCP layer.

**HTTP/3**: uses QUIC (UDP-based) instead of TCP — eliminates TCP head-of-line blocking, faster connection setup (0-RTT), better performance on lossy networks. Each stream is independent so packet loss only affects that stream.
